issues.title: Lazy-initialised perfect hash aggregate table with a bounded bit extension
issues.hypothesis: E0003 showed that perfect hashing q13's inner aggregate (18 bits, 1.53M rows, 150k groups) saves about 25% wall time (115->90ms, agg CPU 0.20s->0.04s). It also showed that estimate-based acceptance fails: q13 is underestimated 5x and q17 overestimated 1000x. q17 regressed because PerfectAggregateHashTable's constructor (perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp:28-48) eagerly calls InitializeStates on all 2^bits slots in every thread, and Combine (:163) and Destroy (:289) walk all 2^bits slots. If states are initialised only on first touch, a perfect table on a near-empty input costs one uninitialised malloc and a memset of 2^bits bool flags, so a cardinality-independent bit cap becomes safe for small inputs.
issues.plan: 1) perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp constructor: keep the uninitialised data allocation and the group_is_set memset, and remove the InitializeStates loop. 2) AddChunk (:132-142): when group_is_set[group] is false, set it to true and append the slot address to a new-groups address vector, then call RowOperations::InitializeStates once for those new slots before UpdateStates. Flag first, so a duplicate in the same chunk is not initialised twice. 3) Combine: when the target slot is not set, InitializeStates the target first (batch new targets the same way), then CombineStates. Add a touched-groups counter as a member in perfect_aggregate_hashtable.hpp, incremented on first touch. If other.touched == 0, return early (still move the allocator). Otherwise scan group_is_set 8 bytes at a time (memcpy into uint64_t and skip zero words). 4) Destroy: call destructors only on slots with group_is_set (only those are initialised). 5) Scan: the same word-skip over group_is_set. 6) plan_aggregate.cpp CanUsePerfectHashAggregate (:230): keep the PerfectHtThresholdSetting check, but also accept when total bits <= 18 and 2^bits * an estimated row width stays below about 8MB per thread. Use a file-local constexpr. Do NOT change the setting's default. Build in the background, check with EXPLAIN ANALYZE that q13's inner aggregate becomes PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY, then run the full bench and look closely at q17, q14 and q18.
issues.expected_gain: q13 about -20% (measured with a forced SET in E0003). Small gains on other GROUP BYs over dense integer keys with 13-18 bits (E0003 quick bench hinted at q02, q03, q07). Geomean maybe 2-3%.
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY on integer keys with a stats range of 4k-262k values (customer, part, supplier and date keys), which is common in analytics. Lazy init also helps existing <=12-bit perfect aggregates on tiny inputs. Could get slower: aggregates with a wide stats range but very sparse actual groups and large inputs (random access over a table up to 8MB instead of a compact HT), and plans with many tiny overestimated aggregates (each pays a 262KB memset per thread).
issues.risk: Medium. Correctness: every state must be initialised before Update, Combine or Finalize, and Destroy must skip uninitialised slots (aggregates with destructors, e.g. list or string min/max). The header change rebuilds a moderate number of files. The 18-bit cap must hold, because 23 bits was measured 10x slower.

output.memory:
## db_evolve planner memory (duckdb)

### Round log
- G1R1: baseline 1.000x, geomean 40.0ms. E0001 (substring-match selectivity) retired because the implementer ran out of time, not because the idea was bad.
- G1R2: E0002, a minimal version of E0001, built OK. Estimates moved (q09 join estimate 1.26M → 241k) but the physical plan did NOT change, so there was no gain. RETIRED. The premise was wrong (see the hash join facts below).
- G2R1: E0003, estimate-based perfect-hash acceptance. RETIRED. With k=2 it never fires on q13 (estimate 300k vs actual 1.53M). With k=8: q13 -24% but q17 +64% (an 18-bit perfect HT on an aggregate estimated at 6M rows that sees 5,850 rows). Geomean only -2.1%. The idea is good; estimate-based gating is the wrong mechanism.
- G2R2: dispatched "Lazy-initialised perfect hash aggregate table with a bounded bit extension": lazy InitializeStates on first touch, Combine/Destroy/Scan over touched slots only, plus a <=18-bit acceptance in plan_aggregate.cpp regardless of the estimate.

### Lessons for dispatching
- Keep diffs out of widely included headers (long rebuilds). Use file-local statics or constexpr.
- Ask implementers to build in the background and to EXPLAIN-check before the full bench.
- CHEAP EXPERIMENTS: `dbe-tool sql "SET <setting>=X; <query>; <query>"` prints per-statement ms (first run cold, second hot). Use it for investigation only.
- rules.md item 4: never change default settings. So the perfect_ht_threshold default (12) stays. Extensions must be an additional acceptance path in code.
- Planner estimates after LIKE filters and outer joins are off by 5-1000x. Prefer runtime-adaptive mechanisms over estimate thresholds.

### Tooling facts
- EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) hangs. EXPLAIN ANALYZE via `dbe-tool sql` works and prints the full plan with timings.
- Use the Grep tool on .dbe/profile.md with pattern `│ +[A-Z_]{5,} +│|[0-9]\.[0-9]+s +│|[0-9,]+ rows +│` to extract operator timings.
- profile.md truncates big plans (q09 lower half, q18 subquery). Operator times are summed CPU, not wall time.

### Codebase facts (verified)
- HASH_JOIN: the LEFT child is the probe and the RIGHT child is the build.
- Join bloom filter: JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:761) works only for single-key joins, because the BF uses the combined hash of all keys (JoinHashTable::InsertHashes, join_hashtable.cpp:717). q09's 2-key partsupp join (800k probe rows) gets only min/max filters. A per-key BF is a medium-size project and the next idea for q09.
- LIKE: LikeMatcher is already good. FSST scan decompresses every row (q13 orders NOT LIKE scan 0.22-0.29s CPU).
- RelationStatisticsHelper::DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY=0.2 is applied flat to non-equality filters.
- Perfect hash agg: CanUsePerfectHashAggregate plan_aggregate.cpp:127, threshold check at :230.
  - PerfectAggregateHashTable (src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp): the constructor InitializeStates all 2^bits slots eagerly (:36-48). AddChunk sets group_is_set (:140). Combine (:163), Scan (:255) and Destroy (:289) loop over all 2^bits slots. The operator is physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp.
  - Measured: q13 inner agg (18 bits): forced perfect hashing 115→90ms wall, agg CPU 0.20→0.04s.
  - Measured: GROUP BY l_orderkey (23 bits, 6M rows): 76ms → 800-1000ms. Keep a cap of 18-20 bits.
  - Measured: a 20-bit perfect table on an empty input costs ~10ms extra on 8 threads (eager init).
- Radix HT adaptation: DecideAdaptation radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424, MaybeRepartition :479.

### Profile hotspots (G2R1)
- q09 118ms, q13 97, q18 83, q19 47, q16 46, q22 42, rest 20-35ms. q17 ~20ms is sensitive to aggregate overhead in its decorrelated subquery.
- q09: hash join probes ~0.24s CPU each, lineitem scan 0.43s.
- q13: orders scan + NOT LIKE 0.22s, RIGHT join 0.10-0.15s, HASH_GROUP_BY 0.20s.
- q18: the cost is in the subquery GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING over 6M rows (~76ms standalone), a radix HT with 1.5M groups.

### Directions
- Active: lazy perfect HT (G2R2). If it regresses q17, check whether the Combine and Scan bool-scan, or the per-thread memset, is the cost. Lower the cap to 16-17 bits before giving up.
- Next: multi-key join bloom filter (q09). High-cardinality radix agg (q18, open backlog issue). q19 OR-filter, q16 and q22 not yet investigated.
- Exhausted: cardinality-selectivity tweaks for q09; estimate-gated perfect hashing.
